tour.name: Ayutthaya Private Day Trip from Bangkok: Temples of the Ancient Capital & Bang Pa-In Palace
tour.subtitle: A private day in the old capital of Siam with a licensed guide and car: the Bang Pa-In summer palace, the Buddha head entwined in tree roots at Wat Mahathat, the three chedis of Wat Phra Si Sanphet, a river lunch, and sunset at Wat Chaiwatthanaram.

tour.overview:
For more than four centuries, from 1350 to 1767, Ayutthaya was the capital of Siam and one of the largest and richest cities in the world, a trading port on an island ringed by rivers, visited by merchants from China, Japan, Persia and Europe. In 1767 a Burmese army besieged and burned it; the court moved south, and the ruins of hundreds of temples were left among the trees. The Historic City of Ayutthaya has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1991.

This private day takes you there from Bangkok with a licensed guide and a car. You stop at the Bang Pa-In summer palace on the way, explore the main temple ruins of the island, have lunch by the river and end at Wat Chaiwatthanaram, the most photogenic of the temples, as the sun lowers.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Bangkok
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 5 km on flat ground, in the heat

WHAT YOU SEE
• Bang Pa-In palace.
• Wat Mahathat.
• Wat Phra Si Sanphet and Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit.
• Wat Lokayasutharam.
• Wat Chaiwatthanaram.

WHY THIS WORKS
The temples are spread across the island and beyond; the car takes you from one to the next in minutes, and we visit the open-air ruins in the morning and late afternoon, when it is cooler.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, photographers and anyone who wants to see Thailand beyond Bangkok.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer markets and canals, choose our floating market tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The ruins are hot and largely unshaded: bring a hat and sun cream. Covered shoulders and knees are required in the temples still in use and at Bang Pa-In. Never pose for photos beside the Buddha head at Wat Mahathat in a way that places your head higher than it.

days.name: Bang Pa-In, Wat Mahathat, Wat Phra Si Sanphet, Wat Lokayasutharam, a river lunch and Wat Chaiwatthanaram
days.description:
What to expect: the ruins of the ancient capital of Siam with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:30 and drive north, about an hour and a half. You first stop at Bang Pa-In, the summer palace founded in the 17th century and rebuilt by King Rama V in the 1870s, a garden of lakes and pavilions in Thai, Chinese, Gothic and Italianate styles, including a Thai pavilion that seems to float in the middle of a pond.

On the island of Ayutthaya, you visit Wat Mahathat, founded in 1374 to hold relics of the Buddha. Its central prang collapsed long ago, and among the headless statues and brick foundations you find the most famous image of Ayutthaya: a stone Buddha head slowly lifted from the ground by the roots of a fig tree, which have grown around it. Your guide explains how to photograph it respectfully, crouching so your head stays lower than the Buddha's. You continue to Wat Phra Si Sanphet, the royal temple inside the old palace grounds, with its three bell-shaped chedis holding the ashes of kings, and next door to Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit, which shelters one of Thailand's largest bronze Buddhas. You also see Wat Lokayasutharam, where a whitewashed reclining Buddha 42 metres long lies in the open air.

Lunch is at a restaurant by the river, with grilled giant river prawns, a speciality of Ayutthaya. In the afternoon you visit Wat Chaiwatthanaram, built in 1630 by King Prasat Thong on the west bank of the river in the Khmer style, its central prang surrounded by towers and a gallery of Buddhas, best seen in the golden light of late afternoon. Your driver takes you back to Bangkok, arriving at about 17:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel in Bangkok.
09:00 – Bang Pa-In palace.
10:30 – Wat Mahathat.
11:30 – Wat Phra Si Sanphet and Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit.
12:30 – Lunch by the river.
14:00 – Wat Lokayasutharam.
14:45 – Wat Chaiwatthanaram.
15:45 – Drive back to Bangkok.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A return by river cruise to Bangkok can replace the drive on some days.
• Bicycles can be rented to explore part of the island.
• We do not include elephant rides, which are offered at some sites; we do not support them.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, palace and temple tickets, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: river cruise, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About an hour and a half each way from central Bangkok, depending on traffic.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Bang Pa-In palace and all the temples in the programme.

faq.question: Is there a dress code?
faq.answer: Yes. Cover shoulders and knees, especially at Bang Pa-In and the temples still in use.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, by the river, often with grilled river prawns. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy exploring the ruins and spotting the Buddha head in the tree. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. Most temples are on flat ground, with some uneven brick paths. The car parks close to each one.

faq.question: Can we return by boat?
faq.answer: On some days, a river cruise from Ayutthaya to Bangkok can replace the drive back; ask us.

faq.question: Do you include elephant rides?
faq.answer: No. We do not support elephant riding. If you want to meet elephants, we recommend an ethical sanctuary in Chiang Mai.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Thailand but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light, covering clothes, a hat, sun cream and comfortable shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to February. From March to May it is very hot; in the rainy season, mornings are usually dry.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
